# Prospekt

> Prospekt is an iPhone lens simulator: a live viewfinder that shows what a 14 to 300 mm lens frames on your camera body. 59 bodies built in, custom bodies, 1.4x and 2x extenders. $3.99 once, no subscription, no account, works offline. iPhone only, iOS 17 or later. It shows framing, not depth of field or bokeh. Made by nakolini (Vitalii Kikot and Dmytro Hryb).

## Pages

- [Prospekt for iPhone](https://prospekt.nakolini.com/): what it does, price, privacy, limits, comparison, FAQ
- [Lens comparison tool](https://prospekt.nakolini.com/lens-compare/): free web tool, frames of any focal lengths and zooms on one or two bodies over a photo, how much of the scene each lens covers at a distance, and how far to stand to fit a subject (metres or feet). The distance calculator is part of the web tool, not the app
- [Cameras](https://prospekt.nakolini.com/cameras/): focal length, full-frame equivalent and angle of view tables for 59 camera bodies, what 24 to 135 mm cover at 1 to 10 m, and portrait distances (full body, head and shoulders)
- [Changelog](https://prospekt.nakolini.com/changelog/): every release
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6760914468)

## Facts

- App Store name: Lens Simulator: Prospekt (localized: Lenssimulator: Prospekt; Objektivsimulator: Prospekt; Simulador Objetivos: Prospekt; Simulador de Lentes: Prospekt; Simulateur Objectif: Prospekt; Simulatore Obiettivi: Prospekt; レンズシミュレーター: Prospekt; 鏡頭模擬器: Prospekt; 镜头模拟器: Prospekt; 렌즈 시뮬레이터: Prospekt)
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6760914468, sold by Vitalii Kikot, co-founder of nakolini
- Version 1.3.2, released 2026-10-03. Site updated 2026-10-10
- Price: one-time purchase, no subscription, no in-app purchases. US $3.99, DE 3,99 €, ES 3,99 €, FR 3,99 €, IT 3,99 €, JP ¥600, KR ￦6,600, NL € 3,99, PL 19,99 zł, BR R$ 24,90, TR ₺199,99, UA 4,99 USD, CN ¥28.00, TW NT$120.00
- Platform: iPhone, iOS 17 or later. No Android or iPad version. Works offline; no account, no analytics, no ads
- What it does: a live viewfinder that crops the iPhone camera to the field of view of a 14 to 300 mm lens on a chosen camera body, with 1.4x and 2x extenders and custom bodies
- What it doesn't do: depth of field, bokeh, distortion or lens rendering. Below about 13 mm equivalent the iPhone's ultra-wide is the limit, and long focal lengths use digital zoom, so they look soft. For cinema cameras and cine lenses, a director's viewfinder such as Artemis or Cadrage fits better
